front: TC020: What is the minimum viable move?
back: Add one small easing clause to your request — "if it's easy" or "no worries if not" — that makes a genuine no just as available as a yes.

front: TC020: What is the core sequence?
back: Reduce the effort: "If it's easy, could you send the link?" -> Reduce the ambiguity: "A yes or no is all I need." -> Give an easy path to reply: "A one-line answer is plenty." -> Make no genuinely acceptable: "No worries at all if not.".

front: TC020: What is the field tip?
back: Easier to answer, not harder to refuse.

front: TC020: What is the strong version of: Can you do this for me? It'll only take a second.?
back: If it's easy and you've got it nearby, could you send the link? If it'd take digging, please leave it.

front: TC020: What is the strong version of: Just following up again — I really need this today.?
back: Whenever suits — a link is plenty, and if someone else is better placed, feel free to pass it on.

front: TC020: What is the strong version of: Have you had a chance to look at my email yet??
back: No urgency — a one-line steer is all I need, and a no is completely fine.

front: TC020: What is better than: "No pressure, but I really need it today."?
back: "If it's easy, today's great; if not, tomorrow's fine."

front: TC020: What is better than: "So sorry to bother you, I know you're slammed, but if you possibly could…"?
back: "Quick one — could you send the link?"

front: TC020: What is better than: The easing line, then straight into pushing your own agenda.?
back: Say "only if it's easy" and mean it, with nothing attached.

front: TC020: What are signs it is working?
back: They reply quickly and easily. They give a little more detail than you asked for. They relax — tone softens, pace picks up. They correct you without any friction. They say "yes", "that's it", or offer a next step. They stay engaged rather than going quiet.

front: TC020: When should you avoid this technique?
back: The ask has real stakes that need a full, honest discussion. Saying no would be socially risky for them.

front: TC020: What is the best recovery line?
back: Sorry, that came out heavier than I meant — please treat it as completely optional.
